# AUD-015: Frontend unit tests fail once the committed deployment is on Sepolia

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | fixed |
| Severity | low |
| Category | other (test isolation / build configuration) |
| Found by (method) | experiment during Phase 5 generation: the full frontend suite run with `addresses.json` set to chain 11155111 |
| Found by (person) | Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5), Phase 5 session, directed by Chordia Laksh |
| Location | `frontend/src/config/networks.ts:3-10` and `frontend/src/test/fixtures.ts:56` at `f943f9c` (Phase 4); exposed by Phase 5 decision D18 at `3be10c0` (`ai-baseline-phase5`) |
| AI session that produced the code | Phase 4 frontend and tests: Codex, 28 October 2026 ([curated summary](../ai-logs/phase4-session.md); no verbatim log). Phase 5 generation that exposes it: Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5), session archived under `docs/ai-logs/raw/` |
| Baseline commit | 3be10c0 (`ai-baseline-phase5`) |
| Regression test commit | 342234a |
| Fix commit | a36b1e9 |

## What is wrong

The app takes its target chain from the committed, generated deployment file:

```ts
// frontend/src/config/networks.ts (Phase 4)
export const targetNetwork = { chainId: deployment.chainId, ... };   // deployment = addresses.json
```

The unit tests' mock wallet is hard-wired to the local chain:

```ts
// frontend/src/test/fixtures.ts:56
chain = "0x7a69";   // 31337
```

Nothing in the test setup pins the deployment. The suite therefore passes only while the committed `addresses.json` says chain 31337. Under Phase 5 decision D18, `addresses.json` keeps the latest deployment and points at Sepolia once the Sepolia deployment is committed. With chain 11155111 in that file, 39 of the 117 existing frontend tests fail: the app treats the mock wallet as being on the wrong network (`docs/evidence/aud-015/frontend-tests-sepolia-config-before.log`, 40 failed including the new regression test).

## 1. Why the AI made the mistake

What the code shows:
- Phase 4 (Codex) wrote the tests against the one deployment that existed, a local one. `fixtures.ts` hard-codes 31337 while `networks.ts` reads the chain from the generated file, and `setup.ts` mocked nothing.
- The Phase 4 report says the generated addresses "identify the validation session" (`docs/phase4-implementation.md`, "Reproducible local workflow"). The coupling was therefore visible, but no test covered a non-local deployment.
- The Phase 5 generation (Claude Code, `3be10c0`) made the change that brings this out. D18 makes the committed file point at Sepolia, and the generation changed `networks.ts` without changing how the unit tests get their deployment. The defect showed up only because the session ran the suite with a Sepolia `addresses.json` as an experiment. Without that run it would have surfaced when the user committed the real Sepolia deployment.

Hypothesis: neither generation treated `addresses.json` as an input that changes by network. Phase 4 had no public-network deployment to test against, and the Phase 5 generation focused on the scripts and the network table.

## 2. Why it is a problem

The failure sequence: the user runs `npm run deploy:sepolia` and commits `addresses.json` and `deployments/sepolia.json` as Phase 5 evidence. From that commit on, `npm test --prefix frontend` fails 39 tests on `main` for every developer. The contracts and frontend code are still correct. This is the evidence the report relies on ("the same contract functionality has passing automated tests locally"). It would either be reported falsely as broken, or someone would "fix" it by reverting the Sepolia configuration. No funds or permissions are at risk.

## 3. How we fixed it

`frontend/src/test/setup.ts` mocks `../config/contracts` for every unit test file. It keeps the real ABIs and replaces `deployment` with the fixed local test values the suite was written against: chain 31337, the same address, block and hashes as the Phase 4 `addresses.json`. The unit tests no longer read the committed deployment. The app code is unchanged. The integration test (`vite.integration.config.ts`) does not use `setup.ts` and deploys its own fixture, so it is unaffected. Fix commit: a36b1e9.

CLAUDE.md rule added (see "Rules learned from audit findings").

## 4. Evidence the fix works

- Regression test: `frontend/src/test/deploymentIsolation.regression.test.ts` :: "targets the local test chain even when addresses.json points at Sepolia". It mocks the committed file as Sepolia and checks that `switchNetwork` asks the wallet for `0x7a69` and that the app's target chain is 31337.
- Before: `docs/evidence/aud-015/frontend-tests-before.log`: 1 failed (the regression test), 117 passed. With a Sepolia `addresses.json`: `frontend-tests-sepolia-config-before.log`, 40 failed and 78 passed.
- After: `docs/evidence/aud-015/frontend-tests-after.log`: 118 passed. With a Sepolia `addresses.json`: `frontend-tests-sepolia-config-after.log`, 118 passed. The production build passes with either file (`frontend-build-after.log`, `frontend-build-sepolia-config-after.log`), and so does the integration test against a local node (`integration-after.log`).
- Contract evidence runs, unaffected because the defect is frontend-only: `docs/evidence/runs/20261105T034657Z_342234a-dirty_AUD-015-before/` and `20261105T035112Z_a36b1e9-dirty_AUD-015-after-rerun/`, both 142 passing. The first after-run, `20261105T035007Z_a36b1e9-dirty_AUD-015-after/`, recorded `gas exit 1`. The cause was `EBUSY: resource busy or locked` on a generated typechain file, not a test failure, and the re-run is clean. "-dirty" refers only to the archived 069871d2 transcript, which another session modified.
- Not verified: the real Sepolia `addresses.json` (none exists yet). The test uses a simulated one.

# Project rules for Claude Code

This repo is graded on two things: the dApp, and how well we audit the code AI tools wrote for it. The process below exists so every claim in our AI Audit Report has evidence behind it. Follow it even when it feels slower.

## Before writing any code

- Read `docs/spec/spec-v1.md` first.
- If it still contains `TODO(decision)` markers, the spec is not frozen. Do not write contract code. Say which decisions are still open and stop.
- Every function you write must trace to a section of the spec. If the spec is silent or ambiguous on something you need, stop and ask. Do not invent requirements.

## Branches and tags

- Never commit to, rebase, or rewrite an `ai-baseline` branch, or move the `spec-v0` or `ai-baseline` tags. The project tags each phase separately: `ai-baseline-phase2`, `ai-baseline-phase3`, `ai-baseline-phase4` and `ai-baseline-d5` are all covered. A new phase gets a new `ai-baseline-<phase>` tag on its first complete AI generation.
- Never amend published commits or force-push.

## When a bug, vulnerability or spec gap is found

1. Run `scripts/new-issue.sh "<short title>"`. This creates `docs/issues/AUD-NNN-*.md`.
2. Write a regression test that FAILS on the current code. Commit it alone as `test(AUD-NNN): ...`.
3. Run `scripts/evidence.sh AUD-NNN-before`.
4. Fix the code. Commit as `fix(AUD-NNN): ...`.
5. Run `scripts/evidence.sh AUD-NNN-after`.
6. Fill in all four sections of the issue file. Do not set Status to fixed without both evidence runs.

In "Why the AI made the mistake", only state what the transcript or code shows. If you are guessing, start the line with `Hypothesis:`.

## Secrets

- Never read `.env` or print private keys, RPC keys or API keys. AI transcripts in this repo are committed to git.
- Only testnet burner wallets are used in this project.

## Commit message prefixes

| Prefix | Use for |
|---|---|
| `ai:` | Code generated by an AI tool and committed with little or no human change |
| `human:` | Code written or substantially rewritten by a person |
| `test(AUD-NNN):` | Regression test for an issue |
| `fix(AUD-NNN):` | Fix for an issue |
| `docs:` | Spec, report, issue files |
| `evidence:` | Evidence runs, testnet logs |
| `chore:` | Tooling and config |

## Rules learned from audit findings

Append a rule here each time an audit finding shows the AI making a mistake it could repeat. Every rule must cite the issue it came from. This section is part of our specification engineering evidence, so never delete old rules; mark them superseded instead.

- AUD-004: A whitelist mapping alone does not restrict ERC-20 movement. Enforce sender and recipient eligibility in OpenZeppelin's transfer hook and execute a direct-transfer regression; skipped tests are not passing behavioral evidence. Apply the latest explicit requirements when revocation semantics differ from the historical spec.
- AUD-005: Before testing an invariant, check it against every later requirements file. If a later requirement makes it false, restate it in the spec in the same change. Never name a test after an invariant unless the test would fail when that invariant is broken.
- AUD-006: A stored `issuer` or owner field is not proof of authority. Test every role path that touches it (grant, revoke, renounce, hand-over) and any state, such as escrowed tokens, that becomes unrecoverable when the role is gone.
- AUD-007: "No `receive`/`fallback`" does not mean "cannot receive ETH": `selfdestruct` and coinbase rewards force it in. For every contract that holds ETH, test forced ETH, and provide a way to recover any balance above what is owed.
- AUD-008: Implement each function against both the §5 function table and the §3 roles table. A role restriction stated only in §3 is still a revert condition.
- AUD-006, AUD-007: Write a regression's behaviour assertion first and await it (e.g. `await expect(tx).to.revert(ethers)`), then assert the error name. A test that fails only because an error or function is missing from the ABI does not show a behavioural failure, and an un-awaited transaction can leak into the next test.
- AUD-009: Preserve multi-transaction form input across public registry refreshes. Separately invalidate account-dependent data on wallet/chain changes; test approval and deposit as two consecutive user actions.
- AUD-010: A receipt timeout is not a failed transaction. Preserve its hash, keep duplicate submission blocked, and verify an actual receipt before reporting success or a revert.
- AUD-011: An `npm ci` that passes proves the lockfile works only on the machine that wrote it. After any dependency change, keep `test/FrontendLockfile.regression.test.ts` passing (every optional dependency has a lock entry). Do not claim a clean install for other platforms unless one was actually run there.
- AUD-012: A passing test suite does not show that the code has room to grow. Before tagging any change to a contract that `AssetFactory` deploys, record the runtime bytecode size of all three contracts against the EIP-170 limit (24 576 bytes) in the evidence. Deploy to public networks only with the optimised `production` profile.
- AUD-013: Adding an event or a new path that emits an existing event changes what every log consumer shows. When a contract change adds either, find each frontend or script that reads that contract's events, and test that it labels the new operation correctly.
- AUD-015: Generated deployment files (`addresses.json`, `deployments/`) change with every deploy and network. Tests must never take their expected chain or addresses from them. Before a change makes a generated file point somewhere new, run the full suite with that file in its new state.
- AUD-014: A fix for one path of a shared risk leaves the risk on every other path. When a fix is scoped to one script, network or profile, list every other path that builds or runs the same code, and test them all, or record each one left open as an issue. Keep the optimizer on in every build profile, because `AssetFactory` embeds two other contracts.

input.content:
# Phase 5: Sepolia deployment and scripted Task 5.1 replay

Date: 4–5 November 2026, Asia/Singapore. Tool: Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5), directed by Chordia Laksh. Authority: [phase5-requirements.md](spec/phase5-requirements.md), the brief verbatim plus decisions D11–D18. No Solidity changed.

**Status:** the tooling is built and verified locally. Nothing has run on Sepolia, in MetaMask or in a real browser yet. The D14 local MetaMask rehearsal, which closes Phase 4 (AUD-002), comes before any Sepolia transaction.

## Decisions

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| D11 | `deploy.ts` deploys an empty main factory (Wallet A is admin) for the live demo. `replay.ts` runs all 12 Task 5.1 steps on its own factory. |
| D12 | Sepolia keys are `SEPOLIA_KEY_A` to `SEPOLIA_KEY_D`, read through `configVariable` from environment variables or the Hardhat keystore. |
| D13 | Scenario 7: the UI blocks it before signing (unchanged). The replay sends it with a fixed gas limit, so a reverted transaction is recorded. |
| D14 | The local MetaMask rehearsal comes first and closes Phase 4. |
| D15 | The frontend runs locally against Sepolia. No public hosting. |
| D16 | The Sepolia read RPC is PublicNode (`https://ethereum-sepolia-rpc.publicnode.com`), which needs no key. `VITE_RPC_URL` overrides it. |
| D17 | Step 12 creates DLP (5,000 units at 0.002 ETH), deposits 1,000, and has C buy 10. |
| D18 | Every persistent deploy writes `deployments/<network>.json` (address, chain ID, block, ABIs). `addresses.json` keeps the latest deployment. |

## What was built (tag `ai-baseline-phase5`, 3be10c0)

| Requirement | Implementation |
|---|---|
| Task 5.2: deploy the factory and assign the admin; D11 | `scripts/lib/phase5.ts` `deployMainFactory`. One transaction from Wallet A, nothing else. |
| Task 5.2: save the address, chain ID and ABIs; configure the frontend; D18 | `writeDeploymentOutputs` writes `frontend/src/config/addresses.json` and `deployments/<network>.json`. `deploy.ts` then syncs the frontend ABIs. `deployments/localhost.json` is gitignored, as local anvil broadcasts were. |
| Task 5.2: "runs the demo setup using testnet wallets"; D11, D13, D17 | `runReplay`: step 0 deploys a separate factory, then steps 1–12 run with 34 on-chain checks. Scenario 7 is first simulated (`staticCall`) to get the reason `RecipientNotWhitelisted`, then sent with a 100,000 gas limit and recorded with its status-0 receipt. Step 3 also whitelists the sale contract, which Phase 3 §3.3 requires. The output goes to `docs/evidence/phase5/replay-<network>-<timestamp>.json`. |
| Keys outside the repository; D12 | `hardhat.config.ts` `sepolia.accounts` holds four `configVariable`s. `chainId: 11155111` is pinned. `.env.example` lists the names. |
| Frontend for Sepolia; D15, D16 | `frontend/src/config/networks.ts` `networkFor()`: chain 11155111 is named "Sepolia testnet" and reads through PublicNode unless `VITE_RPC_URL` is set. |
| Evidence template | [`docs/evidence/testnet-log.md`](evidence/testnet-log.md) |
| Run both locally (work plan) | `npm run replay:ephemeral`, `npm run deploy:ephemeral` and `npm run deploy:local`. The Sepolia variants use the `production` profile (AUD-012). |

Not in the spec, so flagged here: `checkFunding` stops the replay before its first transaction if any wallet cannot pay for its part, and `totalsByWallet` reports gas per wallet. Both serve the work plan's funding estimate and D11's aim of reproducible hashes: a replay that runs out of ETH halfway leaves an incomplete record.

## Local verification

| Check | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `npm test` | 142 passing (132 earlier + 10 in `test/Phase5.scripts.test.ts`) | `evidence/phase5/contract-tests.log` |
| `npm test --prefix frontend` | 117 at the baseline (113 + 4 network tests); 118 after AUD-015 | `evidence/phase5/frontend-tests.log`, `evidence/aud-015/frontend-tests-after.log` |
| Frontend build, root typecheck | Pass | `frontend-build.log`, `root-typecheck.log` |
| `npm run test:integration` against `npm run node` | 1 passed | `integration.log` |
| `npm run replay:ephemeral` | 12 steps, 34 checks passing | `replay-ephemeral.log`, `replay-hardhatMainnet-*.json` |
| `npm run deploy:local` | Writes `addresses.json` and `deployments/localhost.json` | `deploy-local.log` |
| EIP-170 (AUD-012 rule) | AssetFactory 13,545 bytes (55.1%), AssetToken 4,124, AssetSale 3,132, in both profiles | `bytecode-sizes.txt` |
| Mutation check | 5 of 5 valid mutants killed (one malformed mutant recorded as invalid) | `mutation.log` |

Measured replay gas: A 3,018,538 (the factory deployment is 2,973,114 of it), B 4,500,345, C 265,618, D 0. C also pays 0.12 ETH (0.1 CPT + 0.02 DLP).

## Review before merge

This review was done by the session that wrote the code, so it is **not independent**. It covered the diff against phase5-requirements.md and the CLAUDE.md rules, and checked by mutation that the new tests fail when the property each names is broken (AUD-005 rule).

| Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Frontend unit tests took their target chain from the committed `addresses.json`. Under D18 that file points at Sepolia, and 39 tests then fail. | [AUD-015](issues/AUD-015-frontend-unit-tests-fail-once-the-committed-deploy.md), fixed in a36b1e9. CLAUDE.md rule added. |
| Scenario 7 behaves differently on the two network types. In-process, the failing send throws but is mined, and the error carries the hash. Over HTTP with local keys, the send returns and the receipt has status 0. | Handled in `runReplay`. Only the in-process path has been run. |
| D11: does the replay touch the main factory? | No. Tested ("runs on its own factory and leaves the main factory empty"). |

Observations, not changed and not verified on Sepolia:
- **Read-after-write on a load-balanced RPC.** The replay checks state right after each receipt. If `TESTNET_RPC_URL` balances requests across nodes that lag each other, a check could read stale state and stop the replay. The replay stops at the first failed check, and a re-run starts a fresh factory, which costs the gas again.
- **PublicNode's `eth_getLogs` limits are unknown.** The history view already splits block ranges when a provider rejects a large range. Whether PublicNode needs this was not checked.
- **Error wording.** If the Sepolia configuration were wrong, some frontend errors would still talk about a "local chain reset". This is cosmetic.
- **This session's transcript was not archived** by the Stop hook during the session (no `raw/` file appeared). It needs archiving or exporting by hand before the AI-log row's link is valid.

## Task 5.3 coverage

| Case | Automated test (local) | Manual on Sepolia |
|---|---|---|
| Wrong network | `frontend/src/test/wallet.test.tsx` "warns on the wrong network…", `configuration.test.ts` "rejects a wallet on the wrong network…" (mocked wallet) | Yes (checklist) |
| Wallet refuses a transaction | `wallet.test.tsx` "handles wallet rejection", `ui.test.tsx` "reports Rejected by user…" (mocked wallet) | Yes |
| Insufficient ETH | `services.test.ts` "blocks insufficient ETH" (mocked provider) | Yes |
| Inventory exhausted | `test/AssetSale.test.ts` "investor buys more than inventory: reverts"; `ui.test.tsx` "blocks insufficient inventory" | — |
| Zero purchase | `AssetSale.test.ts` "buy of zero quantity reverts" | — |
| Recipient not whitelisted | `AssetToken.test.ts` "rejects an unapproved recipient…"; replay scenario 7 (D13) | Replay plus a UI screenshot |
| Revocation before a transfer | `Phase3.regression.test.ts` "a revoked holder keeps its balance but cannot send, receive or buy…" | — |
| Attacker uses another issuer's admin functions | `AssetFactory.test.ts` "issuer isolation"; `AssetToken.D5.test.ts` invariant 7 tests | — |
| Withdrawal with no funds | `AssetSale.test.ts` "withdrawProceeds with zero balance reverts" | — |
| ETH withdrawal to a contract that rejects it | `AssetSale.test.ts` "a failed payout reverts and leaves the proceeds claimable" | — |

## Not verified

Everything on Sepolia, MetaMask signing, PublicNode reads, any real browser, and the D14 rehearsal. Sepolia transaction hashes go into `docs/evidence/testnet-log.md` once the user has run the scripts.

# AssetToken: Tokenisation Using Blockchain

An academic dApp for NTU SC4053. Authorised issuers tokenise fictional real-world and digital assets as ERC-20 tokens and sell them at a fixed price to whitelisted investors. All ownership records and compliance rules live on Ethereum. The repository is also graded on how the AI-written code was audited, so every change carries an evidence trail (see [Audit trail](#audit-trail)).

**Status (4 November 2026):** contracts, frontend and local tests are complete. Two things remain: a genuine MetaMask browser check ([AUD-002](docs/issues/AUD-002-frontend-dashboards-and-wallet-integration-are-uni.md)) and the public Sepolia deployment ([AUD-003](docs/issues/AUD-003-deployment-and-verification-tooling-are-incomplete.md)).

## What it does

| Contract | Role |
|---|---|
| `AssetFactory` | The platform admin authorises or revokes issuers. An authorised issuer creates an asset, which deploys an `AssetToken` and an `AssetSale` and records them in the registry (`getAsset`, `getAssetCount`). |
| `AssetToken` | A fixed-supply ERC-20 with 0 decimals. Every transfer requires a whitelisted sender and recipient. Revoking an investor keeps their balance but blocks sending, receiving and buying. The issuer can **pause** all token movement and **force-transfer** tokens out of a revoked address, for example to recover a lost key (decision D5). |
| `AssetSale` | Holds sale inventory and sells it at a fixed price, with exact ETH payment. The issuer withdraws proceeds, closes the sale and recovers unsold tokens. ETH forced in from outside can be swept. |

The frontend (React 18, Vite, ethers 6) has a marketplace, an investor portfolio with transfers, issuer and admin dashboards, and on-chain transaction history. The specification is [`docs/spec/spec-v1.md`](docs/spec/spec-v1.md). Where the later phase requirements in [`docs/spec/`](docs/spec/) differ from it, those requirements and their recorded decisions (D1–D10) govern.

## Setup

Validated with Node 22.18.0 (Phase 4 session) and Node 24.15.0 with npm 11.12.1 on Windows. From the repository root:

```bash
npm ci
npm ci --prefix frontend
npm run compile
```

## Run locally

Use three terminals, all started in the repository root:

```bash
# Terminal 1: leave the local blockchain running
npm run node
```

```bash
# Terminal 2: deploy to that persistent chain and sync ABIs/configuration
npm run deploy:local

# Optional: seed CPT/DLT for exploration, only on an empty local registry
npm run demo:local
```

```bash
# Terminal 3: start the frontend
npm run dev --prefix frontend
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:5173**. You can browse without a wallet. To sign transactions, connect MetaMask and switch to **Local Ethereum**: chain **31337**, RPC **http://127.0.0.1:8545**, symbol **ETH**. The app offers to add this network when you ask to switch.

Use Hardhat local accounts 0–4 for the admin, the issuer, investor 1, investor 2 and an unapproved investor. Only import these development accounts into a separate development wallet or profile. Hardhat prints their publicly known keys in your terminal; never use them for real funds or commit them. The application never asks for, stores or reads wallet private keys or seed phrases.

Every deployment writes `frontend/src/config/addresses.json` and syncs the three compiled ABIs. After restarting or resetting the chain, deploy again and restart Vite. The app checks the deployment's block hash and runtime bytecode hash, not just its address. `npm run deploy:ephemeral` deploys to a throwaway in-process chain instead.

The UI has no pause or forced-transfer controls (spec-v1 §7 does not require them). The issuer calls them directly on the token contract. Forced transfers do appear in the transaction history.

## Tests

```bash
npm test                              # 132 contract tests
npm test --prefix frontend            # 113 frontend behaviour tests
npm run build --prefix frontend       # TypeScript + production Vite build
npx tsc --noEmit                      # root scripts and contract tests
npm run test:integration              # needs `npm run node` running; deploys its own fixture
bash scripts/evidence.sh <label>      # build, test, gas, coverage (slither if installed) into docs/evidence/runs/
```

The integration suite runs the production frontend services against real local contracts. It signs through an EIP-1193 adapter over Hardhat's unlocked accounts, so it does not test MetaMask. It covers the full lifecycle, including a forced transfer and a pause. The counts above are from 4 November 2026. Contract line coverage is 98.79%.

## Sepolia deployment

```bash
npm run deploy:sepolia
```

This builds with the optimised `production` profile (AUD-012). Every profile has the optimizer on (AUD-014): unoptimised, `AssetFactory` is right at the 24 576-byte EIP-170 limit, because it embeds the other two contracts. `hardhat.config.ts` reads `TESTNET_RPC_URL` and `PRIVATE_KEY` with `configVariable`, from environment variables or Hardhat's encrypted keystore (`npx hardhat keystore set PRIVATE_KEY`). Nothing loads a `.env` file automatically; [`.env.example`](.env.example) lists the names. Use a testnet burner wallet only.

## Audit trail

AI tools (Claude Code, Codex, claude.ai) generated the contracts, tests and frontend. Commit prefixes record who wrote each change. [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) sets the rules every AI session follows, including rules learned from each audit finding.

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| [`docs/issues/INDEX.md`](docs/issues/INDEX.md) | AUD-001 to AUD-014. AUD-001 to AUD-003 are tracking issues; the rest are defects. Each defect has before/after evidence and an analysis of why the AI made the mistake. Defects from AUD-005 onward, except AUD-009 and AUD-010 (Phase 4, uncommitted at the time), also have a separate failing-test commit and fix commit |
| [`docs/ai-logs/INDEX.md`](docs/ai-logs/INDEX.md) | Every AI session: tool, model, context given and outcome. Transcripts are in `docs/ai-logs/raw/` (emails and Hardhat dev keys redacted, decisions D9 and D10) |
| Tags `ai-baseline-phase2`, `-phase3`, `-phase4`, `-d5` | Each first complete AI generation, never edited afterwards. The pre-AI spec is tagged `spec-v0` in the local repository but has not been pushed |
| [`docs/evidence/`](docs/evidence/) | Evidence runs and per-issue logs |
| [`docs/report/REPORT-MAP.md`](docs/report/REPORT-MAP.md) | Which evidence backs each section of the AI Audit Report |

Commit prefixes show who wrote what: `ai:`, `human:`, `test(AUD-NNN):`, `fix(AUD-NNN):`, `docs:`, `evidence:`, `chore:`. Implementation notes: [Phase 2](docs/phase2-implementation.md), [Phase 3](docs/phase3-implementation.md), [Phase 4](docs/phase4-implementation.md), [D5](docs/d5-implementation.md).

Academic demonstration only. Assets and token prices are simulated. Tokens do not represent legally enforceable ownership or investment claims.

# AssetToken: Tokenisation Using Blockchain

An academic dApp for NTU SC4053. Authorised issuers tokenise fictional real-world and digital assets as ERC-20 tokens and sell them at a fixed price to whitelisted investors. All ownership records and compliance rules live on Ethereum. The repository is also graded on how the AI-written code was audited, so every change carries an evidence trail (see [Audit trail](#audit-trail)).

**Status (5 November 2026):** contracts, frontend and local tests are complete. The Phase 5 Sepolia deployment and replay scripts are built and verified locally ([Phase 5](docs/phase5-implementation.md)). Two things remain: a genuine MetaMask browser check, which is the D14 local rehearsal ([AUD-002](docs/issues/AUD-002-frontend-dashboards-and-wallet-integration-are-uni.md)), and running the deployment on Sepolia ([AUD-003](docs/issues/AUD-003-deployment-and-verification-tooling-are-incomplete.md)).

## What it does

| Contract | Role |
|---|---|
| `AssetFactory` | The platform admin authorises or revokes issuers. An authorised issuer creates an asset, which deploys an `AssetToken` and an `AssetSale` and records them in the registry (`getAsset`, `getAssetCount`). |
| `AssetToken` | A fixed-supply ERC-20 with 0 decimals. Every transfer requires a whitelisted sender and recipient. Revoking an investor keeps their balance but blocks sending, receiving and buying. The issuer can **pause** all token movement and **force-transfer** tokens out of a revoked address, for example to recover a lost key (decision D5). |
| `AssetSale` | Holds sale inventory and sells it at a fixed price, with exact ETH payment. The issuer withdraws proceeds, closes the sale and recovers unsold tokens. ETH forced in from outside can be swept. |

The frontend (React 18, Vite, ethers 6) has a marketplace, an investor portfolio with transfers, issuer and admin dashboards, and on-chain transaction history. The specification is [`docs/spec/spec-v1.md`](docs/spec/spec-v1.md). Where the later phase requirements in [`docs/spec/`](docs/spec/) differ from it, those requirements and their recorded decisions (D1–D18) govern.

## Setup

Validated with Node 22.18.0 (Phase 4 session) and Node 24.15.0 with npm 11.12.1 on Windows. From the repository root:

```bash
npm ci
npm ci --prefix frontend
npm run compile
```

## Run locally

Use three terminals, all started in the repository root:

```bash

npm run node
```

```bash
# Terminal 2: deploy to that persistent chain and sync ABIs/configuration
npm run deploy:local

# Optional: seed CPT/DLT for exploration, only on an empty local registry
npm run demo:local
```

```bash
# Terminal 3: start the frontend
npm run dev --prefix frontend
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:5173**. You can browse without a wallet. To sign transactions, connect MetaMask and switch to **Local Ethereum**: chain **31337**, RPC **http://127.0.0.1:8545**, symbol **ETH**. The app offers to add this network when you ask to switch.

Use Hardhat local accounts 0–4 for the admin, the issuer, investor 1, investor 2 and an unapproved investor. Only import these development accounts into a separate development wallet or profile. Hardhat prints their publicly known keys in your terminal; never use them for real funds or commit them. The application never asks for, stores or reads wallet private keys or seed phrases.

Every deployment writes `frontend/src/config/addresses.json` and syncs the three compiled ABIs. After restarting or resetting the chain, deploy again and restart Vite. The app checks the deployment's block hash and runtime bytecode hash, not just its address. `npm run deploy:ephemeral` deploys to a throwaway in-process chain instead.

The UI has no pause or forced-transfer controls (spec-v1 §7 does not require them). The issuer calls them directly on the token contract. Forced transfers do appear in the transaction history.

# AssetToken: Tokenisation Using Blockchain

An academic dApp for NTU SC4053. Authorised issuers tokenise fictional real-world and digital assets as ERC-20 tokens and sell them at a fixed price to whitelisted investors. All ownership records and compliance rules live on Ethereum. The repository is also graded on how the AI-written code was audited, so every change carries an evidence trail (see [Audit trail](#audit-trail)).

**Status (5 November 2026):** contracts, frontend and local tests are complete. The Phase 5 Sepolia deployment and replay scripts are built and verified locally ([Phase 5](docs/phase5-implementation.md)). Two things remain: a genuine MetaMask browser check, which is the D14 local rehearsal ([AUD-002](docs/issues/AUD-002-frontend-dashboards-and-wallet-integration-are-uni.md)), and running the deployment on Sepolia ([AUD-003](docs/issues/AUD-003-deployment-and-verification-tooling-are-incomplete.md)).

## What it does

| Contract | Role |
|---|---|
| `AssetFactory` | The platform admin authorises or revokes issuers. An authorised issuer creates an asset, which deploys an `AssetToken` and an `AssetSale` and records them in the registry (`getAsset`, `getAssetCount`). |
| `AssetToken` | A fixed-supply ERC-20 with 0 decimals. Every transfer requires a whitelisted sender and recipient. Revoking an investor keeps their balance but blocks sending, receiving and buying. The issuer can **pause** all token movement and **force-transfer** tokens out of a revoked address, for example to recover a lost key (decision D5). |
| `AssetSale` | Holds sale inventory and sells it at a fixed price, with exact ETH payment. The issuer withdraws proceeds, closes the sale and recovers unsold tokens. ETH forced in from outside can be swept. |

The frontend (React 18, Vite, ethers 6) has a marketplace, an investor portfolio with transfers, issuer and admin dashboards, and on-chain transaction history. The specification is [`docs/spec/spec-v1.md`](docs/spec/spec-v1.md). Where the later phase requirements in [`docs/spec/`](docs/spec/) differ from it, those requirements and their recorded decisions (D1–D18) govern.

## Setup

Validated with Node 22.18.0 (Phase 4 session) and Node 24.15.0 with npm 11.12.1 on Windows. From the repository root:

```bash
npm ci
npm ci --prefix frontend
npm run compile
```

## Run locally

Use three terminals, all started in the repository root:

```bash
# Terminal 1: leave the local blockchain running
npm run node
```

```bash
# Terminal 2: deploy to that persistent chain and sync ABIs/configuration
npm run deploy:local

# Optional: seed CPT/DLT for exploration, only on an empty local registry
npm run demo:local
```

```bash
# Terminal 3: start the frontend
npm run dev --prefix frontend
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:5173**. You can browse without a wallet. To sign transactions, connect MetaMask and switch to **Local Ethereum**: chain **31337**, RPC **http://127.0.0.1:8545**, symbol **ETH**. The app offers to add this network when you ask to switch.

Use Hardhat local accounts 0–4 for the admin, the issuer, investor 1, investor 2 and an unapproved investor. Only import these development accounts into a separate development wallet or profile. Hardhat prints their publicly known keys in your terminal; never use them for real funds or commit them. The application never asks for, stores or reads wallet private keys or seed phrases.

Every deployment writes `frontend/src/config/addresses.json` and syncs the three compiled ABIs. After restarting or resetting the chain, deploy again and restart Vite. The app checks the deployment's block hash and runtime bytecode hash, not just its address. `npm run deploy:ephemeral` deploys to a throwaway in-process chain instead.

The UI has no pause or forced-transfer controls (spec-v1 §7 does not require them). The issuer calls them directly on the token contract. Forced transfers do appear in the transaction history.

## Tests

```bash
npm test                              # 142 contract and script tests
npm test --prefix frontend            # 118 frontend behaviour tests
npm run build --prefix frontend       # TypeScript + production Vite build
npx tsc --noEmit                      # root scripts and contract tests
npm run test:integration              # needs `npm run node` running; deploys its own fixture
npm run replay:ephemeral              # the 12 Task 5.1 steps in-process, Hardhat accounts 0-3 as Wallets A-D
bash scripts/evidence.sh <label>      # build, test, gas, coverage (slither if installed) into docs/evidence/runs/
```

The integration suite runs the production frontend services against real local contracts. It signs through an EIP-1193 adapter over Hardhat's unlocked accounts, so it does not test MetaMask. It covers the full lifecycle, including a forced transfer and a pause. The counts above are from 5 November 2026.

## Sepolia deployment (Phase 5)

Four testnet burner wallets play the Task 5.1 roles: A is the platform admin and deployer, B the issuer, C an approved investor and D an initially unapproved investor (decision D12). `hardhat.config.ts` reads `TESTNET_RPC_URL` and `SEPOLIA_KEY_A` to `SEPOLIA_KEY_D` with `configVariable`, from environment variables or Hardhat's encrypted keystore. Nothing loads a `.env` file automatically; [`.env.example`](.env.example) lists the names. `PRIVATE_KEY` is no longer used.

```bash
npx hardhat keystore set TESTNET_RPC_URL    # and SEPOLIA_KEY_A, _B, _C, _D
npm run deploy:sepolia    # empty main factory for the live demo; writes addresses.json and deployments/sepolia.json
npm run replay:sepolia    # all 12 Task 5.1 steps on a separate factory; hashes in docs/evidence/phase5/
```

Both build with the optimised `production` profile (AUD-012). Every profile has the optimizer on (AUD-014), because `AssetFactory` embeds the other two contracts. The replay checks every wallet's balance before its first transaction. The frontend then runs locally against Sepolia (D15) and reads through PublicNode's keyless endpoint (D16); `VITE_RPC_URL` overrides it, but never put a keyed URL there, because Vite compiles it into the browser bundle. Record the results in [`docs/evidence/testnet-log.md`](docs/evidence/testnet-log.md). See [Phase 5](docs/phase5-implementation.md).

## Audit trail

AI tools (Claude Code, Codex, claude.ai) generated the contracts, tests and frontend. Commit prefixes record who wrote each change. [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) sets the rules every AI session follows, including rules learned from each audit finding.

| Tags `ai-baseline-phase2`, `-phase3`, `-phase4`, `-d5` | Each first complete AI generation, never edited afterwards. The pre-AI spec is tagged `spec-v0` in the local repository but has not been pushed |
| [`docs/evidence/`](docs/evidence/) | Evidence runs and per-issue logs |
| [`docs/report/REPORT-MAP.md`](docs/report/REPORT-MAP.md) | Which evidence backs each section of the AI Audit Report |

# AssetToken: Tokenisation Using Blockchain

An academic dApp for NTU SC4053. Authorised issuers tokenise fictional real-world and digital assets as ERC-20 tokens and sell them at a fixed price to whitelisted investors. All ownership records and compliance rules live on Ethereum. The repository is also graded on how the AI-written code was audited, so every change carries an evidence trail (see [Audit trail](#audit-trail)).

**Status (5 November 2026):** contracts, frontend and local tests are complete. The Phase 5 Sepolia deployment and replay scripts are built and verified locally ([Phase 5](docs/phase5-implementation.md)). Two things remain: a genuine MetaMask browser check, which is the D14 local rehearsal ([AUD-002](docs/issues/AUD-002-frontend-dashboards-and-wallet-integration-are-uni.md)), and running the deployment on Sepolia ([AUD-003](docs/issues/AUD-003-deployment-and-verification-tooling-are-incomplete.md)).

## What it does

| Contract | Role |
|---|---|
| `AssetFactory` | The platform admin authorises or revokes issuers. An authorised issuer creates an asset, which deploys an `AssetToken` and an `AssetSale` and records them in the registry (`getAsset`, `getAssetCount`). |
| `AssetToken` | A fixed-supply ERC-20 with 0 decimals. Every transfer requires a whitelisted sender and recipient. Revoking an investor keeps their balance but blocks sending, receiving and buying. The issuer can **pause** all token movement and **force-transfer** tokens out of a revoked address, for example to recover a lost key (decision D5). |
| `AssetSale` | Holds sale inventory and sells it at a fixed price, with exact ETH payment. The issuer withdraws proceeds, closes the sale and recovers unsold tokens. ETH forced in from outside can be swept. |

The frontend (React 18, Vite, ethers 6) has a marketplace, an investor portfolio with transfers, issuer and admin dashboards, and on-chain transaction history. The specification is [`docs/spec/spec-v1.md`](docs/spec/spec-v1.md). Where the later phase requirements in [`docs/spec/`](docs/spec/) differ from it, those requirements and their recorded decisions (D1–D18) govern.

## Setup

Validated with Node 22.18.0 (Phase 4 session) and Node 24.15.0 with npm 11.12.1 on Windows. From the repository root:

```bash
npm ci
npm ci --prefix frontend
npm run compile
```

## Run locally

Use three terminals, all started in the repository root:

```bash
# Terminal 1: leave the local blockchain running
npm run node
```

```bash
# Terminal 2: deploy to that persistent chain and sync ABIs/configuration
npm run deploy:local

# Optional: seed CPT/DLT for exploration, only on an empty local registry
npm run demo:local
```

```bash
# Terminal 3: start the frontend
npm run dev --prefix frontend
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:5173**. You can browse without a wallet. To sign transactions, connect MetaMask and switch to **Local Ethereum**: chain **31337**, RPC **http://127.0.0.1:8545**, symbol **ETH**. The app offers to add this network when you ask to switch.

Use Hardhat local accounts 0–4 for the admin, the issuer, investor 1, investor 2 and an unapproved investor. Only import these development accounts into a separate development wallet or profile. Hardhat prints their publicly known keys in your terminal; never use them for real funds or commit them. The application never asks for, stores or reads wallet private keys or seed phrases.

Every deployment writes `frontend/src/config/addresses.json` and syncs the three compiled ABIs. After restarting or resetting the chain, deploy again and restart Vite. The app checks the deployment's block hash and runtime bytecode hash, not just its address. `npm run deploy:ephemeral` deploys to a throwaway in-process chain instead.

The UI has no pause or forced-transfer controls (spec-v1 §7 does not require them). The issuer calls them directly on the token contract. Forced transfers do appear in the transaction history.

## Tests

```bash
npm test                              # 142 contract and script tests
npm test --prefix frontend            # 118 frontend behaviour tests
npm run build --prefix frontend       # TypeScript + production Vite build
npx tsc --noEmit                      # root scripts and contract tests
npm run test:integration              # needs `npm run node` running; deploys its own fixture
npm run replay:ephemeral              # the 12 Task 5.1 steps in-process, Hardhat accounts 0-3 as Wallets A-D
bash scripts/evidence.sh <label>      # build, test, gas, coverage (slither if installed) into docs/evidence/runs/
```

The integration suite runs the production frontend services against real local contracts. It signs through an EIP-1193 adapter over Hardhat's unlocked accounts, so it does not test MetaMask. It covers the full lifecycle, including a forced transfer and a pause. The counts above are from 5 November 2026.

## Sepolia deployment (Phase 5)

Four testnet burner wallets play the Task 5.1 roles: A is the platform admin and deployer, B the issuer, C an approved investor and D an initially unapproved investor (decision D12). `hardhat.config.ts` reads `TESTNET_RPC_URL` and `SEPOLIA_KEY_A` to `SEPOLIA_KEY_D` with `configVariable`, from environment variables or Hardhat's encrypted keystore. Nothing loads a `.env` file automatically; [`.env.example`](.env.example) lists the names. `PRIVATE_KEY` is no longer used.

```bash
npx hardhat keystore set TESTNET_RPC_URL    # and SEPOLIA_KEY_A, _B, _C, _D
npm run deploy:sepolia    # empty main factory for the live demo; writes addresses.json and deployments/sepolia.json
npm run replay:sepolia    # all 12 Task 5.1 steps on a separate factory; hashes in docs/evidence/phase5/
```

Both build with the optimised `production` profile (AUD-012). Every profile has the optimizer on (AUD-014), because `AssetFactory` embeds the other two contracts. The replay checks every wallet's balance before its first transaction. The frontend then runs locally against Sepolia (D15) and reads through PublicNode's keyless endpoint (D16); `VITE_RPC_URL` overrides it, but never put a keyed URL there, because Vite compiles it into the browser bundle. Record the results in [`docs/evidence/testnet-log.md`](docs/evidence/testnet-log.md). See [Phase 5](docs/phase5-implementation.md).

## Audit trail

AI tools (Claude Code, Codex, claude.ai) generated the contracts, tests and frontend. Commit prefixes record who wrote each change. [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) sets the rules every AI session follows, including rules learned from each audit finding.

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| [`docs/issues/INDEX.md`](docs/issues/INDEX.md) | AUD-001 to AUD-015. AUD-001 to AUD-003 are tracking issues; the rest are defects. Each defect has before/after evidence and an analysis of why the AI made the mistake. Defects from AUD-005 onward, except AUD-009 and AUD-010 (Phase 4, uncommitted at the time), also have a separate failing-test commit and fix commit |
| [`docs/ai-logs/INDEX.md`](docs/ai-logs/INDEX.md) | Every AI session: tool, model, context given and outcome. Transcripts are in `docs/ai-logs/raw/` (emails and Hardhat dev keys redacted, decisions D9 and D10) |
| Tags `ai-baseline-phase2`, `-phase3`, `-phase4`, `-d5`, `-phase5` | Each first complete AI generation, never edited afterwards. The pre-AI spec is tagged `spec-v0` in the local repository but has not been pushed |
| [`docs/evidence/`](docs/evidence/) | Evidence runs and per-issue logs |
| [`docs/report/REPORT-MAP.md`](docs/report/REPORT-MAP.md) | Which evidence backs each section of the AI Audit Report |

Commit prefixes show who wrote what: `ai:`, `human:`, `test(AUD-NNN):`, `fix(AUD-NNN):`, `docs:`, `evidence:`, `chore:`. Implementation notes: [Phase 2](docs/phase2-implementation.md), [Phase 3](docs/phase3-implementation.md), [Phase 4](docs/phase4-implementation.md), [D5](docs/d5-implementation.md), [Phase 5](docs/phase5-implementation.md).

Academic demonstration only. Assets and token prices are simulated. Tokens do not represent legally enforceable ownership or investment claims.

# AUD-003: Deployment and verification tooling are incomplete

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | open |
| Severity | high |
| Category | other |
| Found by (method) | manual code review and command execution |
| Found by (person) | Codex |
| Location | scripts/deploy.ts:10; frontend/package.json:8; tsconfig.json; scripts/evidence.sh; test/, baseline c504215 |
| AI session that produced the code | Unknown; no attribution inferred |
| Baseline commit | c504215 |
| Regression test commit | None |
| Fix commit | None |

## What is wrong

Local deployment throws TypeError at hre.network.provider.request under Hardhat 3. The frontend production build fails with TS5083 because frontend/tsconfig.json is absent. Root type checking includes the frontend without JSX/DOM options and reports invalid Hardhat API usage. All 41 test cases are skipped. The evidence runner invokes absent forge/slither commands and returns exit 0 even though every recorded step exits 127.

## 1. Why the AI made the mistake

The source explicitly labels these areas as future phases. The original generation transcript was not inspected; no causal claim is made.

## 2. Why it is a problem

The application cannot satisfy its frozen specification or support an end-to-end demonstration. A successful compile or zero-exit test command does not establish working behavior.

## 3. How we fixed it

Open; no implementation change made during verification. Required next work: Update deployment for Hardhat 3; add separate frontend/backend TypeScript configuration; implement real tests; align the evidence pipeline with the selected toolchain and propagate failure status.

## 4. Evidence the fix works

No fix or regression result is claimed. See `docs/VERIFICATION.md` for observed command results and limitations.

## Phase 2 follow-up — 23 October 2026

Token tests are now executable; only the 22 factory/sale placeholders remain skipped. This issue remains open for the unrelated frontend, full deployment, root typecheck and Foundry evidence pipeline. Phase 2 runs Hardhat directly and stores command logs under `docs/evidence/phase2/`; see `docs/phase2-implementation.md`.

## Phase 3 follow-up — 23 October 2026

`scripts/deploy.ts` and `scripts/setupDemo.ts` now run under Hardhat 3 (`network.getOrCreate()`) and complete on the in-process network (`docs/evidence/phase3/deploy-local.log`, `setupDemo.log`). The factory/sale placeholders are replaced by 48 executing tests. Still open:
- No Sepolia deployment has been attempted.
- The Sepolia config has one signer, but `setupDemo.ts` needs three.
- ~~No `localhost` network is configured for a persistent node.~~ Wrong (audit-1 F-16): Hardhat 3 provides `localhost` by default.
- ~~`scripts/evidence.sh` still requires `forge`.~~ It has been ported to Hardhat 3: compile, test, gas-stats, coverage, with Slither optional. Each step logs its command and the run records the commit SHA.
- ~~Root typecheck has not been addressed.~~ `npx tsc --noEmit` now exits 0. The frontend is excluded until Vite provides its own tsconfig in Phase 4.
- Still open: Sepolia deployment, and multiple Sepolia signers for `setupDemo.ts`.

## Phase 4 follow-up — 28 October 2026

Persistent `npm run deploy:local` now targets explicit localhost chain 31337 and writes deployment address, block/hash, runtime bytecode hash and all three compiled ABI arrays. The frontend has its own TypeScript/Vite/test configuration and lockfile. Both TypeScript checks, the production frontend build, 112 frontend behavior tests, 108 existing contract tests, actual local frontend-service lifecycle and HTTP route smoke checks pass. See [Phase 4 evidence](../evidence/phase4/README.md). `deploy:ephemeral` retains the throwaway workflow; `demo:local` explicitly seeds the two demo assets only on an empty local registry.

Still open: genuine browser/MetaMask validation, Sepolia deployment and a multi-wallet public-testnet demonstration. No public deployment or interactive pass is claimed; Phase 5 remains outside this task.

## Deferral — 4 November 2026

The Sepolia deployment was attempted on 4 November 2026 and did not run: the project root has no `.env` (only `.env.example`), and no Sepolia RPC endpoint has been provisioned yet. Chordia Laksh deferred the deployment until Phase 5. The Phase 1 roadmap places public-testnet integration inside Phase 5 ("End-to-End Integration & Testing"), so the Phase 5 plan must include it.

Ready now: `npm run deploy:sepolia` builds with the optimised `production` profile (AUD-012, AUD-014). It reads `TESTNET_RPC_URL` and `PRIVATE_KEY` from environment variables or Hardhat's keystore; nothing loads `.env` automatically. The README's "Sepolia deployment" section documents this.

Needed for Phase 5:
- A Sepolia RPC endpoint.
- A funded Sepolia burner wallet for the platform admin.
- Two or more further burner wallets for the issuer and investors. `setupDemo.ts` needs three signers, and the Sepolia network config currently has one.

# Context management
When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

When you have enough information to act, act. Do not re-derive facts already established in the conversation, re-litigate a decision the user has already made, or narrate options you will not pursue. If you are weighing a choice, give a recommendation, not an exhaustive survey

Do build original games, games in a genre or with similar mechanics, and games from the user's own designs and assets. Don't build a recreation of a specific existing game (its name, characters, art, music, levels or look), even if it is renamed or called original.
